text:
anya: Kicking off bring-up for customer Newcrest's stitch adapter (stitch v0.3 merged to main). Quickpack targets: invoice extraction, monetary amounts, and postcode normalization. Running int4 smoke + int8-hybrid contrast. Will paste quick diffs here.

ravi: Nice. Is stitch using the new param layout (stitch_blocks) or plain LoRA keys? Need to know for loader aliasing.

anya: stitch_blocks yes + tokenizer remap -> tcmap2. We didn't update the converter for tcmap2 yet. runtime has alias flag but not enabled by default for customer branches.

carmen: Ran 250-sample quickpack on newcrest-stitch:v0.3 int4. Summary: amount extraction F1 down 1.8% vs baseline, postcode normalization fine, but currency symbol stripping broken for GBP pence values. Example: 
```
input: "Total: £4.50 (incl VAT)"
baseline: "4.50 GBP"
newcrest-stitch:int4: "450.00 GBP"
```
Looks like decimal token got merged into integer token during quantized decode.

anya: Woah. Could be token id shift or byte-level merge at quant. Can you re-run with tokenizer diff and with --no-fast-bpe? Command: 
```
r-infer eval --model newcrest-stitch:v0.3 --quant int4 --prompts quickpack_financials.json --no-fast-bpe --out /tmp/newcrest_int4.json
```
Also run int8-hybrid: 
```
r-infer eval --model newcrest-stitch:v0.3 --quant int8-hybrid --prompts quickpack_financials.json --out /tmp/newcrest_int8hy.json
```

ops-bot: Canary created for newcrest-stitch:v0.3 -> id 9987. 5k tokens queued, p50 72ms, p95 180ms. Canary link: https://ci.redwood/internal/canaries/9987

ravi: I'll diff tokenizer maps baseline <-> tcmap2 and produce a patch if there are id collisions. If we see decimal-split token differences, probably need an alias layer mapping '.'+digits sequences back.

carmen: Re-ran with --no-fast-bpe and int8-hybrid. int8-hybrid results: amount extraction recovered ~0.6pts but still off. Sample: 
```
input: "Amt: 0.75 GBP"
baseline: "0.75 GBP"
int8-hybrid: "0.75GBP"  # missing space in output -> downstream parser failed
```
Seems spacing tokenization merged.

anya: OK. Two failure modes: (1) decimal alignment (token id shift), (2) spacing token being squashed. Both point to tokenizer tcmap2 differences plus quant rounding. Next steps: @ravi to produce token map patch, @carmen to run conversion_shim (adapter_alias=true) + rerun int4. If conversion_shim fixes spacing, we can iterate on quant config (quant bits per group).

perf-bot: Regression alert: newcrest-stitch:int4 candidate shows EM drop 1.8% on quickpack_financials (threshold 1.0%). Alert created: https://alerts.redwood/regs/4521

ravi: If EM >1% we'll block canary rollout. I'll prioritize tokenmap patch. Also suggest adding quickpack_financials to long-term regression suite under tag newcrest-reg-v1.

anya: Agreed. Carmen, post the exact CLI outputs and top 10 failure examples to the eval-run artifact so reviewers can triage. If alias shim closes >80% of failures, we can do a quant-resweep and try different group sizes (gptq group 128 -> 64).

carmen: Uploaded artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/quickpacks/newcrest/9987. Added CSV with failures. Starting conversion_shim run now.

anya: Thanks. Will follow up after conversion_shim run. If we still see decimal merge, we may need to push a tokenizer compatibility layer into the loader for tcmap2 for all customer adapters.

ravi: Patch idea: map token ids for '.' and common two-digit suffix tokens to preserve explicit '.' + digits sequence. Will prototype and run token-diff script: 
```
python tools/token_diff.py --base-tokenizer models/base_tok.json --new-tokenizer models/tcmap2.json --out /tmp/tokdiff.csv
```

anya: Nice. Tagging this: crescent-equivalent? nah 1 newcrest only. Adding owners: @anya (owner), @ravi (tokenizer), @carmen (eval).

perf-bot: Canary 9987 status updated: errors dropped to 0.4% after conversion_shim (prelim). p50 74ms.

anya: Sweet. We'll hold for final run and then decide next steps (block vs staged rollout).
